subject: physics
question_text: Define the critical velocity of a fluid and give its expression.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 15 (printed p.106). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERROR: the source book's expression for the critical velocity names d as the RADIUS of the tube; it is the DIAMETER, because the Reynolds number is defined as Re = ρvD/η with D the diameter — so this card writes D throughout and names it the diameter, not the book's d/radius. Physics hand-checked: v_c = Re·η/(ρD), where Re is the Reynolds number, η the coefficient of viscosity, ρ the density of the fluid and D the diameter of the tube, matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 10.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Say it is the greatest velocity up to which the flow stays streamline; above it the flow turns turbulent.
steps.why: The word critical marks a boundary speed, not a typical one: below it the flow is orderly, and crossing it is exactly what changes the flow's character to turbulent.
common_mistakes: Calling it the speed at which the flow is turbulent. It is the greatest speed at which the flow is still streamline.
Leaving out that flow above this speed turns turbulent.

recall.must_convey: That the critical velocity is the greatest velocity up to which the flow stays streamline, and above it the flow turns turbulent.
accept: boundary between streamline and turbulent flow
reject: v_c equals Re eta over rho D

steps.memory_tip: Critical velocity: the last streamline speed, before the flow turns turbulent.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the expression and name every symbol, with D as the diameter of the tube.
steps.why: The Reynolds number Re is itself defined using the diameter D, so the same D must appear in v_c for the two expressions to stay consistent.
common_mistakes: Calling D the radius of the tube. D is the diameter.
Leaving one of the four symbols unnamed on the right side of the expression.

recall.must_convey: That v_c equals Re times eta over rho D, with Re the Reynolds number, eta the coefficient of viscosity, rho the density and D the diameter of the tube.
accept: v_c is Re eta over rho D
D is the diameter of the tube
Reynolds number times viscosity over density and diameter

steps.memory_tip: v_c = Re·η/(ρD) — D is the diameter, the same D that sits inside the Reynolds number.

insider_note: D is the diameter, not the radius — the printed book calls d the radius here, but the Reynolds number it is built from uses the diameter, so writing D as the diameter is the correction this card makes.
